title: XNNPACK microkernels on RISC-V Vector
task: Port XNNPACK microkernels from ARM Neon to RVV, then optimize, with every candidate gated by upstream tests, bounded formal equivalence, and hardware benchmarks. Deliverables are meant to be submitted upstream.

hardware.development: qemu-riscv64 inside portforge-rvv-host (functional RVV at VLEN 128/256/512/1024; no timing)
hardware.performance: SiFive X280 (RVV 1.0, VLEN 512) via tt-bh-linux on a Blackhole card; OPTIONAL - every gate must also pass with x280=False for sites without the board

gates.xnnpack_tests: candidate registered next to its template kernel; gtest binary green at VLEN 128/256/512/1024 (QEMU) and on the X280 when present
gates.formal_equivalence: cvc5 (SALTyRN harness) ALL_PASSED in configs mode with parameters produced by XNNPACK's own init code, vs the Neon source kernel; integer families are bit-exact, float families use the fixture's FP-aware equality
gates.differential: same digest vs scalar on every platform for families with a driver; new float families need a special-values driver (NaN, +/-0, +/-inf, subnormals)
gates.performance: on the X280 (or FireSim where noted): faster than the scalar ukernel by a clear margin, and not slower than the fastest existing hand-written RVV variant of the family unless the CONTRACT explains why upstream should still want it

anti_cheat: the kernel must handle the full envelope XNNPACK's init can produce, not the test vectors
no reading test sources, fixtures, seeds, or oracle files to special-case values
vector instructions must do the data movement and arithmetic of the hot loop; no scalar fallback that only shifts the loop into the harness
timings are taken as the harness runs them; no warming tricks, no shape detection that changes semantics
deliverable: kernel C file + registry line + (for upstream) generator-template integration, following the layout of the three merged RVV PRs (#9879, #9974, #9996)
